ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect the drive amplifier heatsink fins for dust or blocked ventilation slots. 2. Check the motor body for abnormal surface temperature with a contact thermometer. 3. Inspect the drive amplifier display for thermal warning or fault codes.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect the drive amplifier heatsink fins for dust or blocked ventilation slots. 2. Check the motor body for abnormal surface temperature with a contact thermometer. 3. Inspect the drive amplifier display for thermal warning or fault codes.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Hold a calibrated infrared thermometer or contact thermocouple probe against the drive amplifier heatsink surface after the axis has been running under normal load for twenty minutes. Record the heatsink temperature and compare it against the maximum permitted heatsink temperature stated in the drive amplifier datasheet.

ground_truth.node_text: Hold a calibrated infrared thermometer or a contact thermocouple probe against the drive amplifier heatsink surface after the axis has been running under normal load for 20 minutes. Record the heatsink temperature and compare against the maximum permitted heatsink temperature stated in the drive amplifier datasheet. An overtemperature condition with normal ambient temperature indicates a failed cooling fan or blocked heatsink fins.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Temperature measurement complete. The heatsink is reading sixty-two degrees Celsius, which is below the maximum limit in the datasheet.

ground_truth.node_text: Hold a calibrated infrared thermometer or a contact thermocouple probe against the drive amplifier heatsink surface after the axis has been running under normal load for 20 minutes. Record the heatsink temperature and compare against the maximum permitted heatsink temperature stated in the drive amplifier datasheet. An overtemperature condition with normal ambient temperature indicates a failed cooling fan or blocked heatsink fins.

turns.utterance: Is the drive heatsink temperature within the rated continuous limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Drive heatsink temperature within rated continuous limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Drive heatsink temperature within rated continuous limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the winding resistance balanced within two percent across all phases?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, I'm seeing a variance of about three and a half percent between phase A and phase C.

ground_truth.node_text: Winding resistance balanced within 2% across all phases?

turns.utterance: Inspect the motor terminal block, tighten all connections, and check the insulation condition.

turns.utterance: Terminal block inspected and connections tightened. Insulation looks good with no visible damage.

ground_truth.node_text: Inspect motor terminal block, tighten connections, check insulation

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Inspect the encoder read head status indicator light on the motor body or drive amplifier. Green indicates a valid signal and red or flashing indicates a fault. Check the encoder cable continuity at both connectors using a continuity tester on each signal wire, and inspect the cable route for crush damage, sharp bends, or contact with hot or moving surfaces.

ground_truth.node_text: Inspect the encoder read head status indicator light on the motor body or drive amplifier; green indicates a valid signal and red or flashing indicates a fault. Check the encoder cable continuity at both the motor connector and the drive connector using a continuity tester on each signal wire. Inspect the cable route for crush damage, sharp bends, or contact with hot or moving surfaces.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Encoder status light is showing green. All signal wires have good continuity, and the cable route looks clean with no damage or contact issues.

ground_truth.node_text: Inspect the encoder read head status indicator light on the motor body or drive amplifier; green indicates a valid signal and red or flashing indicates a fault. Check the encoder cable continuity at both the motor connector and the drive connector using a continuity tester on each signal wire. Inspect the cable route for crush damage, sharp bends, or contact with hot or moving surfaces.

turns.utterance: Is the encoder hardware status normal with no fault flags in the drive?

turns.utterance: Is the following error within the specified limit at all three speeds?

turns.utterance: No, the following error is exceeding the limit at fifty percent and ninety percent of rapid traverse rate.

turns.utterance: Adjust the servo gain parameters Kp and Ki within the drive tuning limits.

turns.utterance: Gain parameters adjusted. I've increased Kp by eight percent and Ki by five percent within the allowable range.

turns.utterance: Following error has improved significantly and is now within specification at all three test speeds.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify following error after gain adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the position accuracy within plus or minus zero point zero zero five millimeters at all reference positions?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, all ten reference positions are showing errors well within the plus or minus five micron tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Position accuracy within ±0.005 mm at all reference positions?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the brake holding torque within the rated value?

ground_truth.node_text: Brake holding torque within rated value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The brake is holding, but I'm getting this weird intermittent chattering noise when it engages—like a rapid clicking sound. It's not slipping though, torque seems fine.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, the brake is holding at twelve newton meters, which matches the rated specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Brake holding torque within rated value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Is the axis backlash within the zero point zero zero eight millimeter limit?

ground_truth.node_text: Axis backlash within 0.008 mm limit?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The backlash gauge reads fine, but I'm noticing the ball screw has significant pitting on the thread surfaces and there's metal debris in the lubrication.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, maximum lost motion measured on the dial indicator is zero point zero zero six millimeters, which is within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Axis backlash within 0.008 mm limit?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Are there any significant harmonic peaks in the velocity frequency spectrum?

ground_truth.node_text: No significant harmonic peaks in velocity frequency spectrum?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Actually, I'm seeing a peak at around one hundred eighty hertz that's about seven percent of the mean velocity, which is above the baseline.

ground_truth.node_text: No significant harmonic peaks in velocity frequency spectrum?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Investigate the speed ripple source. Check for bearing issues or encoder pitch error.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Investigation complete. The frequency corresponds to the encoder pitch, suggesting a minor encoder irregularity but within acceptable limits for operation.

turns.utterance: Log all drive parameters and test data.

turns.utterance: All parameters and test results have been logged in the diagnostic report.

turns.utterance: Update the drive parameter backup and maintenance management system service record.

turns.utterance: Parameter backup saved and service record updated in the maintenance management system.

turns.utterance: Procedure complete. The servo axis diagnostic has been successfully finished and all findings have been documented.
